top.line: How a person gets their own agentic cell: a key in the browser, a vault they fill, the factory, and their own Claude.

in-short.line: People ask for sites; the workflow is the product; key; their vault; five designs; own Claude; three gates.

why.line: The sites are cheap; collecting, designing and handing over is what costs, so build the workflow.
why.para: Briefed by mistake in PrompTugal, written up there.

ask.line: A start page, a key pair in the browser, and a signed request on an append lane, with no secrets.
ask.para: The worst anyone can do is send a request.

approve.line: The intake agent checks signatures and lists requests; I approve each with one tap.

welcome.line: A message sealed to their key with a template vault, their lane and a key scoped to one vault.

vault.line: A guided app in their vault for photos, words, links, style and signed consent; then sealed to the factory.

merge.line: The factory writes a request; I merge; the apply workflow makes the repository, address and site.

designs.line: One factory session makes five designs, back into their vault, and they choose.

handover.line: A GitHub invitation I approve, and a CLAUDE.md for the owner; they continue in their own Claude.
handover.para: The invite made by a workflow, not a session.

security.line: Sealed keys, signed requests, read keys only, signed consent, a security review, ten free cells.

limits.line: A plan, a pilot scoped key, and a GitHub hand-over still to check.

sources.line: The PrompTugal conductor's plan from my brief, and earlier articles.
